text: Bedlam means wild, noisy chaos. It comes from Bethlem, a London hospital known for its disorder. Here it describes the confusion of banks, flights and government networks failing in the same week.
Frenetic means frantic and wildly fast. Here it describes companies rushing to patch software flaws all at once, a rush that can itself cause problems.
Wayward means straying off in an uncontrolled direction. Here it pictures an AI that has slipped out of human control, which the article says there is little evidence of.
Happenstance is chance, something that happens by accident rather than by plan. In Goldfinger's saying, one odd event is happenstance, but a pattern means someone is behind it.
Eponymous describes the person a thing is named after. Goldfinger is the eponymous villain because the novel is called Goldfinger.
Goldfinger is the villain of Ian Fleming's 1959 James Bond novel, later a famous film. His line about 'enemy action' is quoted here to capture the suspicion that the outages were no accident.
Adrift means drifting without direction, like a boat with no anchor or oars. Here office workers were left with no way to do their jobs.
A glitch is a small, sudden fault in a machine or program. Here a glitch in radio communications stopped flights across the country.
Signals intelligence means spying by intercepting electronic messages, such as phone calls and emails. It is the NSA's main job.
The NSA is the American government agency that collects foreign electronic communications and protects government networks. Its own secret communication system was disrupted.
Classified means officially secret, shared only with people who have clearance. A classified system holds government secrets.
The homeland security secretary leads the department that guards the US against terrorism, cyber-attacks and border threats.
A spate is a sudden run of similar events, such as a spate of break-ins. Here it means several outages in a few days.
Self-fixing describes software that repairs itself without people. The article's quote marks show the claim comes from a secondhand theory, not an expert.
The FAA is the US agency that regulates flying and runs air-traffic control.
A router is a device that directs data between computers or networks, like a traffic cop for internet messages. A new one caused the air-traffic problem.
Josh Hawley is a Republican senator from Missouri who often criticises big institutions. Here he demands a briefing for the whole Senate.
To 'buy' an explanation is slang for believing it. Senator Hawley does not believe the officials' story.
Mayhem is violent or chaotic disorder. Here it describes a week of digital breakdowns.
Malicious means done on purpose to harm. Malicious hackers break into systems to cause damage or steal.
Tinkering means fiddling with something, making small changes. Even careful tinkering with old systems can break them.
Fraught means full of risk or trouble. Changing old, complex computer systems is fraught because a small change can cause surprising failures.
Vulnerabilities are weak spots in software that attackers could use to break in. Finding and fixing them is called patching.
Paradoxically means in a way that seems to contradict itself. Here, work meant to make systems safer is creating new risks.
Prosaic means ordinary and unexciting. A prosaic explanation, like a faulty router, is dull rather than dramatic.
El Dorado is a small city in Arkansas. Its name is Spanish for 'the golden one', after a legendary city of gold.
Amarillo is a city in the Texas Panhandle, where a radar site is located.
Fibre-optic cables carry data as pulses of light through thin glass strands. They are much faster than old copper wires.
Newfangled means new and unfamiliar, often said a little doubtfully. Here it refers to AI systems.
To pony up is slang for paying money that is owed or demanded. The secretary wanted Congress to hand over $50bn.
A patch is a small update that fixes a flaw in software. Here a July patch hid a bug that appeared months later.
Rolled out means released to users step by step, as in a new feature being rolled out.
To crop up means to appear unexpectedly. The bug cropped up only months after the patch.
Inadvertently means by accident, without meaning to. Data from two systems landed on one network by accident.
To keel over means to fall or tip over suddenly, like a boat capsizing. Here servers collapsed.
Cascading means spreading step by step like a waterfall or dominoes. A cascading failure is one small fault that triggers many others.
JPMorganChase is the largest bank in the United States.
Chris Krebs was the first head of CISA, the US cyber-security agency, and is a respected voice on digital safety.
Commonalities are shared features. The events differ but have things in common, like efforts to be safer.
Mark Warner is a Democratic senator from Virginia who helps lead the Senate Intelligence Committee.
Unprecedented means never seen before. AI can find flaws at a speed with no earlier match.
Anthropic is an AI company that makes the Claude models and also built Mythos.
Mythos is an Anthropic AI model that is very good at finding and exploiting software flaws, so it is both useful for defence and risky.
Glasswing is the programme that gives chosen firms special access to Mythos to fix their code first.
To exploit a flaw means to use it to attack. Exploiting a vulnerability can let a hacker take control.
Bad guys is casual speech for criminals or enemies, here hackers.
Volume is how much and velocity is how fast. Together they describe a flood of fixes arriving quickly.
A CVE is a public catalogue number for a known software flaw. Counting CVEs shows how many flaws are found.
Staggering means shockingly large. Over 5,000 fixes in a year is staggering next to about 4,000 in three years.
To strip something bare means to remove everything useful. Layoffs might leave firms without staff who understand their systems.
Layoffs are job cuts by an employer, usually to save money.
To conjure is to call something up, as a magician does. Each incident conjures fears of an attack.
The Soufan Centre is a research group on security and terrorism.
Living in someone's head rent-free means being on their mind constantly without earning it. Americans think about foreign enemies all the time.
Whopping is informal for very large. A $6.3bn theft is whopping.
Binance is one of the world's largest cryptocurrency exchanges.
Swept out means cleared away entirely, like dust from a room. Flaws would be removed.
Scant means barely any. Scant comfort means almost none.
